The Yjs, Automerge and Loro columns were decided from their repositories as cloned on 2026-10-23 — Yjs `main` at 0e0dc34 (14.0.0-rc.29; npm `latest` is still 13.6.33), Automerge `main` at 5bae775 (3.5.0) with automerge-repo at 3ab7c33 (2.6.0-alpha.5), Loro `main` at 75e4bf2 (1.17.1) — and their official docs; where a claim was cheap to test, the published package was run. The syncom column is this repository.

version.note: Branch `features/enhance-crdt-engine-part2`. 0.0.1 is a development placeholder, so there is no npm `latest` to differ from.

license.text: MIT, every subpath included; wrpc, the transport, MIT too
license.note: Every block is a subpath of the one package, MIT like the rest: sync, the storage backends, undo, branches, presence and the ProseMirror and CodeMirror bindings.

impl.text: pure JavaScript: CommonJS, no build step

deps.note: `@alexify/wrpc` is a devDependency only: the application hands its client in.

runtimes.text: node.js ≥ 22 (CI on 22 and 24); browsers through OPFS or IndexedDB
runtimes.note: Nothing in the repository tests or claims Deno, Bun or React Native. The browser half needs Web Crypto with Ed25519, and OPFS or IndexedDB (`@alexify/syncom/idb`).

types.text: hand-written, `tsd`-tested; records typed from the entity's Standard Schema or `Schema<Shapes>`

apiStyle.text: async methods by record id; live `Record` objects stage edits and `save()`
apiStyle.note: Every read and write returns a promise; a write resolves once its op is in the log.

unit.text: a record: a JSON object with an id, many per storage
unit.note: Each top-level field of a record is one kind — register, counter, set, list, text or tree. A replica is a storage directory: records, the op log, the chain, the catalog.

manyDocs.text: a storage holds records by id, in collections, with queries

kinds.text: register, counter, OR-set, list (movable), text (with marks), tree

nesting.text: fields by path (`profile/city`), each of any kind; a list element or a tree node holds fields under its id

roots.text: by field name: the first op decides the kind (`inc`, `add`, `splice`, `treeMove`)
roots.note: A record is created by `insert()` (a minted UUID) or `set(id)`. Two nodes that create one field with the same kind at once merge into one field — there are no container ids; two `set(id)` of one id are whole-record writes and the newer wins.

values.text: JSON only; other values pass through `JSON.stringify` (`Date` → string)
values.note: Checked in a probe: a `Date` reads back as an ISO string, a `Uint8Array` as an object of indexes, `NaN` and `Infinity` as `null`, a field set to `undefined` is dropped, a `BigInt` throws a `TypeError`. There is no binary type.

nestedPlain.text: one register: replaced whole, the newer writer wins
nestedPlain.note: Two nodes changing different keys of one nested object at once keep one side (probe confirmed); `update({ 'a.b': 1 })` writes a field named `a.b`.

kindClash.text: fixed precedence, not stamps: register > counter > set > list > text > tree
kindClash.note: Where the winner arrives the loser's state is dropped; where the winner is held the loser's op is refused (`OP_REFUSED` error event). The loser's ops stay in the log, so `history()` on a node that applied them still shows them.

schema.text: entity schemas, injected validator (Standard Schema, a function, `compile`)
schema.note: Validates local writes (defaults folded into the op) and every peer's op (an invalid one is skipped here, still relayed); schema versions with a lens and `migrate()`.

replicaId.text: `nodeId`: with `/signing`, the Ed25519 public key (43 base64url characters); without it, what `getId` mints

idReuse.text: one open per directory (lock); `SELF` and `REWOUND` caught at hello
idReuse.note: A host refuses a hello from its own id (409 `SELF`), and a node whose stream a host holds more of is told `REWOUND` and moves past it. Two live copies writing at once mint the same seqs: whichever op arrives second under a seq is dropped as a duplicate.

author.text: `actor` on every op (`open({ actor })` or per write), signed and replicated
author.note: A claim the origin signs, not a proof of who the user is.

opId.text: `(origin, seq)` per origin and scope stream, plus its stamp `ts`
opId.note: Vector keys are `origin@scope`; list and text elements are named `ts:offset:origin`, runs `ts:origin`; a log position is an event id `<epoch>.<seq>`.

clock.text: hybrid wall clock `max(Date.now(), last + 1)` that observes peers; vectors for delivery
clock.note: Registers order by `(ts, origin)`. The clock never runs backwards nor behind a stamp it has seen, so convergence does not depend on clocks agreeing — only who wins does.

wallTime.text: always: each op's `ts` is milliseconds and the merge order
wallTime.note: Skew changes who wins, never whether nodes agree; a stamp more than `sync.maxSkew` (24 h) ahead is refused as malformed.

versionRepr.text: a version vector `{ 'origin@scope': seq }` as JSON; event ids, stamps, tags
versionRepr.note: `get(id, { at })` takes an event id (`'<epoch>.<seq>'`, a position in this node's log), a stamp, `{ vector }` or `{ tag }`.

lww.text: per field by `(ts, origin)`: the wall-clock stamp, then the node id

conflicts.text: no multi-value register; a lost value is readable only in history

deleteKey.text: `unset(id, fields)`: an `unset` op, a tombstone an older concurrent `set` loses to

clear.text: `set(id, {})` or `delete(id)`: a reset; newer concurrent ops survive
clear.note: The reset drops what is stamped below it in every kind: registers, counters, set tags, list and text runs, tree moves.

keyOrder.text: as each node's object took the keys; replicas can differ
keyOrder.note: In a probe a whole-record write merged with a concurrent update read `{ only, later }` on one node and `{ later, only }` on the other. A set field reads sorted by element JSON.

counter.text: `inc(id, key, value)`: one running sum per origin, added up

counterNum.text: finite floats; a negative `inc` decrements; each origin's sum within ±2^53−1
counterNum.note: An `inc` that would take its origin's sum past `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is refused as a bound (`detail: 'counter'`), the same on every node; the sums add up in origin order, so fractions read alike everywhere.
counterNum.source: src/ops.js (MAX_COUNT, counterValue, the inc branch); docs/guide/sync.md#guarantees-and-limits

counterReset.text: a reset drops increments stamped below it; a register outranks the counter
counterReset.note: A peer's register write takes the field whatever its stamp (locally `update()` of a counter throws `FIELD_KIND`). A counter one origin incremented both before and after a concurrent reset does not converge — documented and left so.

set.text: oR-set field: `add()` / `remove()`; a concurrent add survives a remove
set.note: A remove names the add stamps its node observed; elements are told apart by their JSON text and read sorted.

listAlgo.text: Fugue (Weidner & Kleppmann 2023), not FugueMax; movable per Kleppmann 2020
listAlgo.note: The placement rule is adapted from `fugue-simple` (MIT); the movable list follows Loro's MovableList.

interleave.text: never: each writer's run stays whole, forward and backward
interleave.note: Tested for forward runs, backward runs (typing at the start) and the Yjs-interleave case (`xab`, never `axb`). Two runs anchored after one element may swap order — the FugueMax difference.

listRange.text: `splice(id, key, index, count, items)`: one op for both

listSet.text: `setAt(id, key, index, value)`: a value register per element, newer stamp wins
listSet.note: The value follows the element through a concurrent move.

listMove.text: `move(id, key, from, to)`; two concurrent moves leave the element once
listMove.note: At the newer move's place (tests and probe).

moveDelete.text: the move wins: the element comes back at the new place
moveDelete.note: The removal took the old slot, the move made a new one; a removal made after the move takes the element away (probe confirmed).

listNested.text: an element holds fields of any kind under its id: `items/<element>/title`, `items/<element>/body` a text

rle.text: content run-length encoded; a writer's next keystroke extends its own run
rle.note: `["ab", 3, "c"]`: items alternate with tombstone lengths (list-positions' form); an extension adds no key to the record.

textAlgo.text: Fugue, the same engine as lists (`src/text/sequence.js`)

textUnits.text: UTF-16 code units, as `String#slice` counts them; no other units

surrogates.text: refused: an index between the halves of a pair is `SURROGATE`; `updateText` diffs by code points

splice.text: `splice(id, key, index, count, text)`; past the end is `OUT_OF_RANGE`

updateText.text: `updateText(id, key, text)`: Myers over UTF-16, one splice per hunk
updateText.note: Diffed inside the mutation queue after the common prefix and suffix; past 1 000 edit steps it is one splice replacing the middle.

delta.text: `toDelta(changes)` and `applyDelta(id, key, delta)`: Quill's form, embeds and marks included

embeds.text: `insertEmbed(id, key, index, { type, attrs })`: a slot (U+FFFC) whose marker is a register, marked like a character

longText.text: a persistent rope, O(log n) per keystroke; the B4 trace (260k edits) in about 6 s, 8 MB of JS heap after it

markExpand.note: `'after'` is the default; `unmark` uses the reversed rule.

markOverlap.text: `{ many: true }` marks stack, each with its own id and value
markOverlap.note: Without `many`, one value per name and character: the newest covering mark (Peritext's `allowMultiple` rule).

unmark.text: `unmark(range, name)` is a null mark; the newer stamp wins against a mark
unmark.note: A stacking mark goes only by its id: `unmarkById()`.

markWinner.text: the newest stamp `(ts, origin)` covering the character

blocks.text: block markers in the text (`splitBlock`, `joinBlock`, `updateBlock`, `blocks()`), `{ type, parents, attrs }`

editors.text: `/prosemirror` and `/codemirror` (the editor's modules injected), `/editor` for any editor through a three-function adapter

cursor.text: `cursor(id, key, index)` → a string; `index(id, key, cursor)` reads it back

cursorValue.text: a string (`<elem`, `>elem`, `^`, `$`) to keep or send

cursorDeleted.text: the next visible element; `null` once a reset (or `compact`) dropped it
cursorDeleted.note: In a list a cursor anchors the slot, not the element: a move leaves it behind.

tree.text: tree field: `treeMove(id, key, node, parent, { after | before })`, `treeRemove`

treeCycle.text: Kleppmann et al. 2021: moves fold in stamp order, the cyclic one skipped
treeCycle.note: The older move stands on every node; the lost move is kept and can count later. Locally a move under a descendant throws `CYCLE`.

treeOrder.text: ordered: a fractional index per move, ties broken by stamp

treeDelete.text: `treeRemove` moves it under `$trash` with its subtree; moving it out restores it
treeDelete.note: A move into a subtree removed concurrently is hidden with it (probe).

treeData.text: a node holds fields under its id (`outline/<node>/title`); the tree reads as `{ id, data, children }`

txn.text: `transact(fn)`: several writes, several records, one log append, all or none

autoCommit.text: every call: durable once its op is appended to the log
autoCommit.note: `open({ defer })` lets record files lag; the log is written at once.

commitMeta.text: `message` (≤ 1,024 characters, signed, replicated), `actor`, `ts`, the schema `v`; no free-form fields

origin.text: a `source` per write and per transaction, on the `commit` and `transaction` events (local); `actor` replicates
origin.detail: The plan named it `origin`; it stays `source`, because a syncom op's `origin` is the node id.

multiDoc.text: `transact(fn)` writes several records as one append, all or none

preCommit.text: `hooks.beforeWrite(ctx)`: return new `data` or throw to refuse
preCommit.note: Runs inside the mutation queue before the op is stamped; an entity validator then folds defaults into the op.

veto.text: `beforeApply` returning `false`, or a failing validator, skips it here
veto.note: A skipped op is still logged and relayed. A host refuses outright what is out of scope, malformed, skewed, forged, or unsigned under `'require'`.

events.text: every op reports `changes` in the write API's terms and the reading's indices; one `transaction` event per turn

eventBody.text: the op and its `changes`; `commit` adds `before` / `after` copies and the kinds; `transaction` the turn's changes by record

localRemote.text: `via` is `null` for a local op; `commit` fires for local ops only

patches.text: `diff(id, from, to)` → JSON patches in the write API's terms
patches.note: One per field by kind (`put`, `inc`, `add`, `remove`, `splice`, `treeMove`…); a text's marks are not diffed.

applyPatches.text: `applyPatches(id, patches)`: new ops, rehearsed, all or none on a refusal

pathSub.text: `observe(id, path, listener)`: the changes of a field, of what hangs under it and of a prefix of it

eventTiming.text: once the op is durable: listeners called synchronously, before the write resolves
eventTiming.note: Listeners are contained: a throw is logged and never fails the write.

historyKept.text: the op log, bounded by retention (10,000 ops by default; `retention: 'all'` keeps everything)

historyList.text: `history(id, { limit, before })`: versions with type, origin, actor, fields, data
historyList.note: Per record, newest first, 50 by default; `log.entriesOf(id)` gives the raw entries.

timeTravel.text: `get(id, { at })` by event id, stamp, vector or tag; `at(tag)` views

timeTravelNeeds.text: the retained log: a fold of the record's ops, exact from a reset
timeTravelNeeds.note: Once compaction ran, a version is exact only from a reset stamped above `droppedTs`, else `HISTORY_GONE`; the cost is one `applyOp` per retained op of the record. A tag costs a copied file per record changed after it.

versionDiff.text: `diff(id, from, to)` between any two versions, as patches
versionDiff.note: Marks are not diffed, and a list's moves come back as splices.

revert.text: `restore(id, at)`: new ops that lead back, whole or not at all
revert.note: A text's marks are not restored, since they are not diffed.

tags.note: Local to the node: tags do not replicate.

blame.text: `lastEditorOf(id, field)`, `editorsOf(id)`, and per element `editorOf(id, key, index)` → `{ origin, ts }`

trim.text: log retention drops old segments; `compact(id)` rewrites a record's metadata
trim.note: Before what compaction dropped a version is `HISTORY_GONE`, and a peer behind the floor bootstraps from a snapshot. `compact()` lays a text's marks again; it names the elements anew, so old cursors read `null` and a stacking mark has a new id.

purge.text: `purge(id)` scrubs the payload from the log here and on every peer it reaches
purge.note: A purge wins at any stamp; signatures and digests stay so the headers still verify, and the tags drop their copies. Per record, not per field; a peer that never comes back keeps what it had.

fork.text: `branch(parent, { path })` (`@alexify/syncom/branch`): a new storage, new identity
fork.note: The fork has its own key pair and log, and forks the whole storage, not one record.

forkAt.text: `branch(parent, { from: { at } })`: an event id, a stamp or a vector, exact while the log retains it

mergeBack.text: `merge(source, { into })`, either way, as ops through `applyRemote`
mergeBack.note: Joins as state when the source compacted past what the other needs (`joined: true`).

detached.text: views of the past are read-only; edit through `restore()` or a branch at any version

suggestions.text: none; a branch (`/branch`) merges back whole

undoLocal.text: this node's own commits only; an undone `add` revokes its own adds alone

undoGroup.text: `mergeInterval` (500 ms), a transaction is one step, `group(fn)`, `mark()` closes a step, `limit` 100

undoScope.text: `trackedSources`, `records` and `paths`: a stack over what they name, the inverse kept to those fields

undoCursor.text: a step's `meta` keeps the application's cursor tokens and travels to its redo; `position()` restores the selection

undoConflict.text: skipped (refuse to overwrite); `force` overrides; counters and sets commute
undoConflict.note: A peer's edit of the same list or text blocks undoing it; a whole-record step with a conflict is skipped whole.

format.text: JSON: `{ entries, hash }` log files of keyed `{ seq, op, fp }`; 19-slot arrays on the wire

spec.text: `docs/reference/wire.md`: the 19 slots, codes, payloads, signed header, files, procedures, bounds

snapshot.text: `snapshot()` pages records with their merge meta; `mergeSnapshot()` joins them
snapshot.note: State without history, tombstones included; `at(tag).snapshot()` pages a past state.

incremental.text: a push sends ops past the host's vector; `changes` resumes from an event id
incremental.note: `log.since(eventId)` is the public reader; the selection by vector (`src/sync/outbound.js`) is internal.

mergeUpdates.text: `mergeEntry(a, b)` joins two record states with no storage
mergeUpdates.note: Ops need no merging: a batch is a list deduplicated by `(origin, seq)`, and `applyOp(entry, op)` is pure too.

jsonExport.text: everything is JSON: snapshot pages, log entries, ops

fastLoad.text: records load by id into a bounded cache; each one parsed whole
fastLoad.note: A catalog file indexes ids, and a sequence's index is cached per entry; no lazy or columnar encoding.

compat.text: a written policy (slots appended, a new type a `PROTOCOL` bump); unpublished, so no version kept yet

syncProto.text: built in: `hello`, `push`, `changes`, `snapshot` over an injected link

reconnect.text: vectors and log epochs at hello, then ops past the vector; the feed resumes
reconnect.note: The subscription resumes from the saved last event id; a node below the host's log floor bootstraps from a snapshot. Duplicates are dropped by vector.

outOfOrder.text: a gap in one origin's stream is dropped and fetched again
outOfOrder.note: Across origins, a list or text op whose anchor has not arrived is held as pending work, 4 096 per field.

duplicate.text: idempotent: the vector drops it, counted in `duplicates`; no event

transport.text: an injected `SyncLink`; `@alexify/syncom/wrpc` for WebSocket and WebRTC
transport.note: Messages are JSON values over call and subscribe, not raw bytes; WebRTC goes through wrpc's peer links. No BroadcastChannel adapter.

server.text: no separate server: any storage hosts with `sync.unit()` on wrpc
server.note: The host checks `authorize`, scopes, push limits, op shape, skew and signatures, and runs its own validators and hooks.

storage.text: built in: `node:fs`, OPFS, IndexedDB (`/idb`), `/memory`, `/layered`, encrypted at rest (`/encryption`), or an injected `fsi`

awareness.text: `/presence`: a state per node, signed, renewed and expired, relayed by a host's rooms, never logged

partial.text: scopes: a `scope()` per record, peers granted scopes, the host enforcing
partial.note: A subset of records, never part of one.

hashes.text: with `/chain`, a per-node hash-linked chain of applied writes, checked on cold reads

signatures.text: with `/signing` (in `/all`): Ed25519 per op, the node id is the key, verified on receipt

checksums.text: every log file carries an xxHash32 of its entries; a signed SHA-256 digest per op with `/signing`

malformed.text: dropped and counted, never thrown: not logged, not relayed (a gap)
malformed.note: A payload `applyOp` cannot admit — of any op type — is `OP_REFUSED` (malformed) and logged as a no-op; a page that throws is retried from its cursor.

bounds.text: pending work, run and field slots, tree depth and index, counter range, skew, push limits
bounds.note: `pendingMax` 4 096 per field (snapshot blocks too), a run 2^20 and a field 2^22 slots, trees 512 levels and 1 024-character indexes, an origin's counter sum ±2^53−1, `maxSkew` 24 h, per-peer `opsPerPush`, `bytesPerPush` and `opsPerSecond`. Nothing else caps a set's size or a tree's move count.

remoteValidation.text: the entity validator and `beforeApply` run on every peer's op

e2ee.text: no; an encrypted record stays local and does not sync

fuzz.text: seeded mesh fuzz: 4 nodes, 80 ops of every kind; a hazard walk
fuzz.note: Also every arrival order of small op sets in the op, sequence and tree tests. The fuzz compares the blocks and move logs, not only the reading; one seed each.

proofs.text: none; cites the papers, and `INVARIANTS.md` maps each guarantee to tests

errors.text: `SyncomError` with a `code` (44 codes); `TypeError` for a wrong argument

devtools.text: `/inspect`: a record's anatomy raw; `stats()`, an injected logger, OpenTelemetry; no visual inspector

anonymize.text: `anonymize(value, { salt, keys })` from `/inspect`: every string hashed, the shape kept

frameworks.text: `/store`: a query, a record or a presence as one store — Svelte's contract and React's `useSyncExternalStore`; Vue and Solid wrap it

docs.text: VitePress site: guides, API reference, architecture, benchmarks

version.note: v14 renames the package to `@y/y` and publishes release candidates under the npm `beta` tag; the README still says `npm i yjs` and documents mostly the v13 API.
version.detail: publish.yml publishes `require(./package.json).name` with --tag beta when the version contains a hyphen. The commit is a shallow clone of main.

status.text: v14 release candidate; v13 is the stable line
status.note: The shallow clone has no CHANGELOG or tag history, so the first release year is not shown; the YATA paper it implements dates from 2016.
status.detail: compatibility.tests.js:5 mentions documents generated with Yjs v13.2.0.

license.text: MIT; y-protocols, y-indexeddb, y-leveldb and y-crdt also MIT
license.source: yjs/LICENSE:1-5; yjs/package.json:68; yjs/README.md:1453-1455; y-crdt/LICENSE:1-5; y-protocols@1.0.7/package.json (license); y-indexeddb@9.0.12/package.json; y-leveldb@0.2.0/package.json
license.detail: README.md:1455 says "Yjs and all related projects are MIT licensed". The providers were checked in their npm package.json files; editor bindings are not cloned.

maintainer.note: yrs/y-crdt is co-maintained by Bartosz Sypytkowski, Kevin Jahns and John Waidhofer.
maintainer.detail: LICENSE copyright also names RWTH Aachen i5. y-crdt/README.md "Maintainers" section.

impl.text: pure JavaScript (ESM source, JSDoc types), no build step
impl.detail: exports "." default is ./src/index.js; `npm run dist` only emits .d.ts via tsc.

deps.detail: lib0 supplies encoding, delta, schema and observable modules.

wasm.text: not used: pure JS; `ywasm` is a separate Rust build

bindings.text: Rust `yrs`, JS `ywasm`, C `yffi`; Python, Ruby, .NET, Swift, Kotlin on yrs
bindings.note: yrs 0.28 follows the v13 type set (`Text`, `Map`, `Array`, `Xml*`) and both update formats, not v14 `Y.Node`.
bindings.detail: pycrdt, yrb, yr, ydotnet, yswift, ykt are separate y-crdt-org repos (not cloned). yrs/src/types has array.rs, map.rs, text.rs, xml.rs, weak.rs; yrs/README.md:62-63 lists update formats v1 and v2. Go ports (ygo, go-yjs) are third-party.

runtimes.text: ESM only; Node ≥ 22 and browsers; CI on Node 26
runtimes.note: Deno, Bun, React Native and workers are not mentioned. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) the package ships CommonJS and ESM builds and needs Node ≥ 16.
runtimes.detail: Browser tests run by hand through test.html (npm run debug); CI runs lint + node tests only.

types.text: generated `.d.ts` from JSDoc; generic `Y.Node<DConf>` types attrs and children
types.note: The type parameter is a compile-time shape only: `$node` checks the name at runtime, not the content.
types.detail: DConf is a lib0 DeltaConf (attrs, children, text, name).

apiStyle.text: mutable shared objects; every call synchronous
apiStyle.detail: No promises in the core API; Doc.whenLoaded/whenSynced are provider hooks.

unit.text: `Y.Doc`: named root nodes plus nested subdocuments
unit.detail: A Doc holds `share` (root nodes by name), the StructStore (all items and tombstones, pending updates) and `subdocs`.

manyDocs.text: subdocuments: a `Y.Doc` as a value, addressed by `guid`
manyDocs.note: Loading and syncing each subdocument is the provider's job; the docs say official providers treat subdocs as separate entities.
manyDocs.detail: funding.json names a planned provider "Titanic" for syncing millions of docs; no code in the clone.

kinds.text: one `Y.Node`: attrs (map), children (list or text), formats, name
kinds.note: v14 folds `Y.Map`, `Y.Array`, `Y.Text` and the XML types into `Y.Node`. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) they are separate classes. Neither has a counter, set, tree or movable list.
kinds.detail: renderer.md:53: "In Yjs v14 all shared types (text, array, map, xml) are instances of the unified Y.Node."

nesting.text: any node holds nodes in its attrs and its children
nesting.note: A node instance lives in one place; to place it elsewhere, insert a `clone()`.

roots.text: `ydoc.get(key)`: roots by name, no create op; same node everywhere
roots.note: A v14 root has one kind, so replicas cannot disagree on its type. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) `getMap('r')` on one replica and `getText('r')` on another each see only their own kind's content (checked by running it). Roots cannot be deleted.
roots.detail: Items under a root encode the root key as a string parent; the receiver resolves it with doc.get(key).

values.note: How `Date` and `bigint` round-trip depends on lib0 1.x `writeAny`, which is not cloned. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) a `Date` reaches peers as `{}` while the writer still reads a `Date`, and a `bigint` wraps to signed 64 bits.
values.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src): 2n**64n-1n arrives as -1n, 2n**70n as 0n, new Date(0) as {}. v14 nodeMapSet accepts Number/Object/Boolean/Array/String/Date/BigInt/Uint8Array/null/undefined; lists also take ArrayBuffer.

nestedPlain.note: Inserted JSON is not copied; in development mode it is deep-frozen, and the docs warn against mutating it.

kindClash.text: one node wins by `clientID`; the loser and its content are deleted
kindClash.note: In v14 both sides are `Y.Node`s, so this is the ordinary register conflict. The loser is reachable only from a snapshot taken with `gc: false`.
kindClash.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: Y.Map (client 1) vs Y.Text (client 2) at one key -> both replicas keep the Y.Text, the map is deleted and empty. Item.integrate is identical between 13.6.33 and the clone except type names.

schema.note: The JSDoc says to validate content as a value, e.g. `delta.$delta(conf).check(node.toDelta())` (lib0 schema); nothing checks remote changes.

replicaId.text: `doc.clientID`: random 53-bit integer, new per `Doc`; app may set it
replicaId.note: Every new `Doc` (each session) gets a new id, so state vectors grow with sessions.

idReuse.text: regenerates on seeing its own id; replicas may already have diverged
idReuse.note: Ops already written under the shared id are dropped as known by the other side, so the replicas end up different for good; the FAQ warns of permanent corruption.
idReuse.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: two docs with clientID 7 typing "AAA" and "bb" end as "AAA" and "bbA"; only the second regenerated its id.

author.text: no: the app maps `clientID`s to users
author.note: In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) the experimental `PermanentUserData` maps them inside the document.

opId.text: `ID(client, clock)` per element; a run shares one item
opId.note: Deletes get no id: the clock counts inserts only.

clock.text: per-client counters (state vector); no Lamport merge, no wall time
clock.note: Concurrent order comes from YATA's `origin`/`rightOrigin`, ties broken by `clientID`. The README calls ids Lamport timestamps, but a client's clock never jumps on receive.
clock.detail: store.getClock(own) is the count of own structs; nothing observes remote clocks.

wallTime.note: Time is used only locally, by `UndoManager` capture grouping and awareness timeouts.

versionRepr.text: state vector (client → next clock), varint binary; snapshot adds deletes
versionRepr.note: The README says the state vector describes local state and is not used to track causality.
versionRepr.detail: Answers the row titled "A version" (crdt-rows.json duplicates the id "version").

versionCmp.note: An app compares decoded state vectors itself.

map.note: Also `clearAttrs`, `attrKeys`, `attrValues`, `attrEntries`, `attrSize`, `forEachAttr`. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) the map is `Y.Map` with `set`/`get`/`delete`/`has`/`clear`.

lww.text: the unseen concurrent write with higher `clientID` wins, not wall-clock
lww.note: A write that saw the other always wins over it; only truly concurrent writes fall to the `clientID` order.
lww.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: client 2 beats client 1.

conflicts.text: losing values are deleted, not readable
conflicts.note: With `gc: false` a lost value stays in the store and shows in an older snapshot, but there is no conflicts API.

deleteKey.text: `deleteAttr(key)`; a concurrent set survives the delete
deleteKey.note: A delete removes only the value it saw; a concurrent set is a new value it never covered.
deleteKey.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: client 5 deletes k while client 3 sets k -> k is set on both.

clear.text: `clearAttrs()`: deletes visible keys in one change; concurrent sets survive
clear.note: There is no whole-document clear, and roots cannot be deleted.

keyOrder.text: local `Map` insertion order; can differ between replicas
keyOrder.note: `toJSON()` returns a plain object, so integer-like keys come first there.
keyOrder.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: client 1 sets a, client 2 sets b -> keys [a, b] on one replica, [b, a] on the other.

counter.note: A number in an attr is a register: concurrent increments lose all but one.
counter.detail: grep for counter/inc in yjs/src finds nothing.

set.text: no set type; map keys behave add-wins
set.note: The docs suggest no model; keys with a dummy value work because a concurrent set beats a delete.

listAlgo.text: YATA (Nicolaescu, Jahns et al., 2016) with an added `originRight`
listAlgo.note: A formal model of YATA exists in the third-party lean-yjs project, cited by the README.

interleave.text: two runs stay whole, forward or backward; a three-replica case interleaves
interleave.note: Not tested in the repo. Run on 13.6.33 (same `Item.integrate`): two writers typing forward or backward at one spot never interleave, but with three replicas a concurrent insert can land inside a right-to-left run.
interleave.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: "xabcDEFy" (forward), "xcbaFEDy" and "helloWORLD" (backward, two writers); replica 3 inserts b, replica 1 inserts a before it, replica 2 concurrently inserts x at 0 -> "axb". The three-replica scenario follows the one published with the Fugue paper (fugue/yjs-interleave), re-run here against yjs itself.

listSet.text: no in-place assign; delete and insert
listSet.note: Two replicas replacing one element concurrently leave both new values in the list.

listMove.note: A move existed only on a side branch of yjs (y-crdt README); main has none. A moved element is delete plus re-insert.
listMove.detail: grep for move in yjs/src finds only "remove".

listNested.text: children may be nodes: lists of maps of texts

rle.text: consecutive inserts by one client merge into one item
rle.note: Deleted runs and garbage-collected ranges merge too.

text.text: text is a node's string children: `insert`, `delete`, `format`, `toString`
text.note: Text, embeds and child nodes can share one node's children. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) the type is `Y.Text`.

textAlgo.text: the same YATA list engine as lists

textUnits.text: UTF-16 code units; no other unit in the JS API
textUnits.note: yrs defaults to UTF-8 byte offsets and can be set to UTF-16 (`OffsetKind`).

surrogates.text: a split pair becomes two U+FFFD; no error
surrogates.note: The document stays valid, but the character is lost on every replica.
surrogates.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: inserting inside an emoji gives "a�X�b"; deleting half of it leaves one U+FFFD.

updateText.note: Editor bindings compute the edits; `applyDelta` takes the result.
updateText.detail: lib0 delta has a diff used internally for renderer switches (ynode.js:859); not documented as a text diff.

delta.note: v14 uses lib0's delta (ops carry `type`, attrs and nested `modify`), not Quill's JSON. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) `Y.Text` reads and applies Quill-style deltas.

embeds.text: JSON objects or nodes inside text

longText.text: one item per typed run; B4 (105k chars): 160 KB doc, 3.2 MB heap
longText.note: Benchmarks are for 13.6.11 (crdt-benchmarks, by the same author); B4×100 (10.5M chars) encodes to 16 MB. A per-keystroke update averaged 29 bytes in 13.3.0.
longText.detail: crdt-benchmarks README line 345: avgUpdateSize 29 bytes (13.3.0). Position lookups use up to 80 cached search markers, disabled once a text has formatting (Item.js:1151-1156).

marks.note: Formats are start/end markers in the list; `null` clears a key.

markExpand.text: none: an insert carries only the formats it names
markExpand.note: Read from the code (not run): unnamed formats at the spot are set to `null`. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) `Y.Text.insert` without attributes inherits the formats on its left.
markExpand.detail: 13.6.33 types/YText.js:1124-1142 copies pos.currentAttributes when attributes are omitted.

markOverlap.text: one value per key at any position
markOverlap.note: Overlapping comments need distinct keys, e.g. one key per comment id.

unmark.text: `format(i, n, { key: null })`; marker order decides against a concurrent mark

markWinner.text: the marker later in list order wins; ties by `clientID`, not time

blocks.text: named child nodes (`new Y.Node('p')`), or Quill-style newline formats

xml.note: In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) these are `Y.XmlFragment`, `Y.XmlElement`, `Y.XmlText`, `Y.XmlHook`; v14 still decodes them.

editors.text: y-prosemirror (Tiptap, BlockNote), y-quill, y-codemirror, y-monaco; Lexical native
editors.note: Bindings live in their own repos (not cloned); which already target v14 is not visible here. Third-party: slate-yjs, y-ace; BlockSuite and Superdoc bind natively.

cursor.note: v14 adds converters between lib0 delta positions and relative positions.

cursorSide.text: `assoc`: ≥ 0 sticks to the next element, < 0 to the previous

cursorDeleted.text: the gap where the element was; `null` once collected
cursorDeleted.note: It follows undo's re-inserted copies by default (`followUndoneDeletions`), which only the undoing peer can see.
cursorDeleted.detail: A deleted Item counts as length 0, so the index is that of the next visible element; a GC struct (parent deleted) returns null.

tree.text: no movable tree; third-party `yjs-orderedtree` builds one on maps
tree.note: Nested `Y.Node`s form a tree, but a node cannot move: it is deleted and a clone inserted.

treeOrder.text: no movable tree; nested nodes' children are an ordered list

treeDelete.text: no movable tree; deleting a node deletes its subtree
treeDelete.note: For nested nodes: an insert into a concurrently deleted node is deleted on arrival; undo can re-create a deleted node.

treeData.text: no movable tree; a nested node carries its own attrs

txn.text: `doc.transact(fn, origin)`: one event round, one update for peers
txn.note: No rollback: if `fn` throws, the edits made so far stay and are sent.
txn.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: a throw after map.set keeps the value and emits one update.

autoCommit.text: each call outside `transact` is its own transaction
autoCommit.note: Nested `transact` calls join the outer one; the update is emitted when it ends.

commitMeta.text: nothing travels with a change; `transaction.meta` is local

origin.text: `transact(fn, origin)`, `applyUpdate(doc, u, origin)`; local only, not replicated
origin.note: Origins reach observers, the `update` event and `UndoManager.trackedOrigins`.

multiDoc.note: Third-party `y-utility` offers undo across docs, not atomic changes.

preCommit.text: no veto; `beforeObserverCalls` sees the applied change
preCommit.note: Observers may add edits in a follow-up transaction, but cannot cancel one.

veto.text: no way to reject part of a remote update
veto.note: The threat model calls server-side update filtering an antipattern and suggests a separate fork for untrusted writers.

eventBody.text: lib0 delta (`event.delta`, `deltaDeep`), changed keys; `update` gives bytes
eventBody.note: In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) map events also list each key's `oldValue` in `event.changes.keys`.
eventBody.detail: v14 YEvent: target, currentTarget, transaction, keysChanged, childListChanged, adds(), deletes(), getDelta({ renderer, deep }).

patches.text: deep lib0 deltas with nested `modify`/`modifyAttr` per change
patches.note: `node.delta` is a maintained live copy of the deep state.

applyPatches.text: `node.applyDelta(delta, origin)` turns a delta into ops
applyPatches.note: It returns a corrective delta when part of the input addressed rendered-but-deleted content.

pathSub.text: observe a node or its subtree; no path filter
pathSub.note: `getPathTo(parent, child)` computes a path for an event target.

eventTiming.text: synchronously when the outermost transaction ends, before `update`
eventTiming.note: Edits made by observers run as further transactions, one after another.
eventTiming.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: order observer > afterTransaction > update > call returns.

historyKept.text: no change log; default GC drops deleted content
historyKept.note: The doc keeps current state plus tombstone ids. With `gc: false` deleted content stays, but not when or by whom.

historyList.note: Per-client insert ranges are available (`createInsertSetFromStructStore`), not grouped into changes.

timeTravel.note: v14 adds `SnapshotRenderer` to render the doc as it was.

timeTravelNeeds.text: `gc: false` and a snapshot captured then; restore rebuilds a doc
timeTravelNeeds.note: A past version cannot be named afterwards: deletes carry no clock, so only snapshots the app kept can be restored.
timeTravelNeeds.detail: createDocFromSnapshot throws if originDoc.gc is true, writes every struct up to the snapshot, and applies it to a new Doc.

versionDiff.note: Arbitrary versions need docs for both (e.g. from snapshots). In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) diffs come from `Y.Text.toDelta(snapshot, prevSnapshot)`.

revert.note: No `revertTo(version)`; the app computes the ids changed since a version, and the code warns it may fail with GC on.

tags.text: no named versions; snapshots are bytes the app stores

blame.text: v14 attribution renderers; who did what is the app's map of `clientID`s
blame.note: Yjs records only `clientID`s; mapping changes to users is collected by the app or server, e.g. from each update's `createContentIdsFromUpdate`. In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) only the experimental `PermanentUserData`.

trim.text: GC drops deleted content; tombstone ids and positions stay
trim.note: No shallow snapshot. A collected doc can no longer restore snapshots.

purge.text: default GC drops deleted content here and on peers that GC
purge.note: A peer with `gc: false`, or stored raw updates not yet compacted, keep the bytes; `mergeUpdates` keeps the first encoding it sees.
purge.detail: y-indexeddb@9.0.12 compacts after 500 stored updates (PREFERRED_TRIM_SIZE) through encodeStateAsUpdate of the collected doc.

fork.text: `Y.cloneDoc(doc)`; the clone is a new `Doc` with a new `clientID`
fork.note: In 13.6.33 (npm `latest`) there is no `cloneDoc`: `applyUpdate(new Y.Doc(), encodeStateAsUpdate(doc))`.

forkAt.detail: The fork shares item ids with the source, so its edits merge back as ordinary updates.

mergeBack.text: exchange updates; `DiffRenderer` accepts or rejects suggestions selectively

detached.text: no checkout; a past version is a new `Doc`, edited as a fork

suggestions.text: `DiffRenderer` keeps a suggestion doc; `acceptChanges`/`rejectChanges` by range
suggestions.note: New in v14; the threat model recommends a separate doc for suggestion-only users.

undoLocal.text: tracks origins in `trackedOrigins` (default `null`); peers' changes stay
undoLocal.note: An update applied without an origin has origin `null` and is tracked as local; providers pass themselves as origin.
undoLocal.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: applyUpdate without origin then undo() removes the remote text; with origin "provider" it stays.

undoScope.text: scope of nodes or a whole doc; `trackedOrigins`, `deleteFilter`

undoConflict.text: keeps peers' later edits; skips a key a peer overwrote
undoConflict.note: `ignoreRemoteAttributeChanges` lets undo overwrite a peer's attr change.
undoConflict.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: local set, remote overwrite, undo -> the remote value stays.

format.text: binary updates: V1 (default) and V2 (columnar, RLE per field)

spec.text: no written spec; the code defines the format
spec.note: yrs reimplements both formats, a second implementation to read against.
spec.detail: Searched yjs, yjs-docs and y-crdt for a format specification; none.

snapshot.note: Yjs keeps no history to leave out; deleted content is included only with `gc: false`.

incremental.text: `encodeStateAsUpdate(doc, stateVector)` sends what that peer lacks
incremental.note: The whole delete set always goes along.

jsonExport.text: `decodeUpdate`/`logUpdate` show structs for inspection; no JSON import

fastLoad.text: compact V2 columns; loading decodes everything, no lazy load
fastLoad.note: Subdocuments are the way to load parts on demand. B4 parses in 39 ms (13.6.11, crdt-benchmarks).

compat.text: no written promise; tests decode v13.2 documents
compat.note: v14 reads v13 updates; it writes new nodes with the XML type refs, so a v13 reader sees them as `Y.XmlFragment`/`Y.XmlElement`.
compat.detail: Inference from _legacyTypeRef (ynode.js:737,2059-2068); not run against a v13 reader.

syncProto.text: `y-protocols/sync`: step 1 state vector, step 2 diff, updates

reconnect.text: state vectors; the reply resends missing items and the full delete set

outOfOrder.text: held as pending and applied when the missing parts arrive
outOfOrder.note: v14 also stores gaps in one client's stream as skips. Pending data is re-sent by `encodeStateAsUpdate`.

duplicate.text: idempotent: no event, no observers; the cost is a decode
duplicate.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: applying one update twice emits one update event.

transport.text: transport-agnostic bytes; official y-websocket, y-webrtc providers
transport.note: Providers are not cloned; many third-party ones exist.

server.note: Not cloned, so described from the README only; the threat model calls server-side update filtering an antipattern. Third-party: Hocuspocus, y-sweet, y-redis.

storage.text: official y-indexeddb and y-leveldb; others third-party
storage.note: Both store updates and compact them after 500.

partial.text: per document via subdocuments; `intersectUpdateWithContentIds` filters by ids
partial.note: No sync of a subtree per peer; the FAQ splits data into docs where permissions differ.

hashes.text: ids are client and clock; no content hashes

malformed.text: throws a plain `Error`; parts decoded before the failure stay applied
malformed.note: Items are integrated before the delete set is read, so a truncated update leaves its items in the doc.
malformed.detail: Checked by running yjs@13.6.33 (bench/compare/node_modules/yjs/src); the code path is unchanged in the clone: an update cut by its last byte throws "Unexpected end of array" after "hello" was applied and an update event fired.

bounds.text: no limits on size, depth or pending data
bounds.note: The decoder sizes arrays from wire counts; the threat model leaves size limits to the app.

e2ee.text: none in core; `y-webrtc` encrypts signaling with a shared secret

fuzz.text: 5 peers, random disconnects and delivery order, up to 100,000 ops
fuzz.detail: 60 randomized cases. compare() checks values, struct stores, delete sets, state vectors, snapshots and a doc rebuilt from mergeUpdates; `npm run test-extensive` repeats for 10 s per case.

proofs.text: third-party lean-yjs (Lean) proves parts of YATA
proofs.note: The README says preservation and commutativity are proven so far and that the paper's pseudocode has errors.

errors.text: plain `Error` messages, no classes or codes

devtools.note: Other devtools listed (y-sweet, Liveblocks, Velt) are third-party.

anonymize.text: `obfuscateUpdate` replaces content, keeps the CRDT structure

frameworks.text: third-party only: react-yjs, SyncedStore, valtio-yjs, immer-yjs

docs.text: docs.yjs.dev: guides, API, ecosystem, internals, for v13
docs.note: v14's `Y.Node` API is in JSDoc and two repo notes; the site and most of the README describe v13.

tests.text: 338 cases in 16 files (lib0/testing); CI on Node 26
tests.detail: 60 of them are randomized `testRepeat*` cases; JavaScript only. y-crdt adds Rust, wasm and FFI tests.

version.note: The clone's main already carries unreleased APIs under the 3.5.0 label (`maskAuthor`/`revealAuthor`), which the npm 3.5.0 build lacks. automerge-repo is read at 3ab7c33 (2.6.0-alpha.5); npm `latest` there is 2.6.0-alpha.3.
version.detail: Checked the installed npm 3.5.0 (syncom/bench/compare/node_modules/@automerge/automerge/dist/implementation.d.ts): no maskAuthor/revealAuthor/isAuthorMasked exports, which exist at automerge/javascript/src/implementation.ts:863-893 on main.

status.text: stable: 3.x since July 2025, 2.0 in Jan 2023; LICENSE from 2019
status.note: automerge-repo, which the sync, storage and framework rows lean on, has an alpha (2.6.0-alpha.3) as its npm `latest`.
status.detail: The repository does not show the first public release (the original JS Automerge predates this repo); the oldest date visible is the 2019 LICENSE copyright. README: 'A stable release of the javascript package is available'.

license.text: MIT: core, WASM, JS, C, automerge-repo and its adapters
license.note: One core file, `text_diff/myers.rs`, is copied from the `similar` crate under Apache-2.0 (its LICENSE sits beside it). The ProseMirror/CodeMirror bindings and Keyhive are outside the clones.

maintainer.text: Ink & Switch; Alex Good and Orion Henry work on it full time
maintainer.detail: package.json collaborators: Orion Henry, Martin Kleppmann. automerge-repo author: Peter van Hardenberg. LICENSE copyright: Ink & Switch LLC (JS, WASM, repo); 'the Automerge contributors' (root).

impl.text: Rust core compiled to WASM (wasm-bindgen), TypeScript wrapper with proxies

deps.text: 0: no `dependencies`; the WASM binary ships inside the package
deps.detail: package.json has only devDependencies (line 83); the installed npm 3.5.0 package.json has no dependencies field either.

wasm.text: required: 3.6 MB `.wasm` (1.1 MB gzip), loaded per export condition
wasm.note: The default `import` inlines the WASM as base64 and instantiates it synchronously; Node reads the file; the `browser` condition needs bundler WASM support (webpack `asyncWebAssembly`, Vite `vite-plugin-wasm` + top-level await); `/slim` + `initializeWasm()` is the manual async path. The repo has no CSP note; on Cloudflare Workers a doc cannot be created outside a handler.
wasm.detail: Measured on the installed 3.5.0: dist/automerge.wasm 3,644,225 bytes, gzip -9 1,136,563 bytes; the base64 module is 4.9 MB.

bindings.text: Rust crate and C API in repo; docs list Python, Swift, R
bindings.note: Python (automerge-py) and Swift (automerge-swift) are automerge-org projects outside the clones; R is community-maintained (CRAN); Go (automerge-go) is named in the 2.0 blog; `samod` is a Rust automerge-repo.

runtimes.text: Node (CI tests 18), browsers, Workers (`workerd`), Deno; React Native via docs recipe
runtimes.note: No `engines` field; automerge-repo needs Node ≥ 22.13. Deno has WASM tests but no CI job; React Native needs Metro package-exports config plus manual init; Bun is not mentioned.
runtimes.detail: packaging_tests: node_cjs/esm fullfat/slim, vite_*, webpack_*, iife, workerd, workerd_slim. CJS bundle built with esbuild target node14 (scripts/build.mjs:401).

types.note: The WASM layer's types are a hand-written TS block in `automerge-wasm/src/lib.rs`, copied to `wasm_types.d.ts` at build. `load<T>` does no runtime check of `T`.

apiStyle.text: immutable doc; `change(doc, d => …)` mutates a proxy, returns a new doc; synchronous
apiStyle.note: Every core call is synchronous except WASM init. A doc handed to `change` becomes outdated and cannot be changed again (`clone` first). automerge-repo wraps it in a `DocHandle` (`handle.change`, events); `repo.find()` is async.

unit.text: a document: one root map tree plus its full hash-linked change history

manyDocs.note: The core holds one document per instance; there are no subdocuments.

kinds.text: map, list, text (with marks and block markers); `Counter` as a scalar
kinds.note: `Table` survives only as a legacy alias of map. No tree, movable list, set or XML type.

nesting.text: any depth: maps and lists hold maps, lists and texts; root is a map
nesting.note: A text holds characters and inline block-marker maps only. `from([1, 2])` gives a map with keys '0' and '1' (probed).

roots.text: one root map; children created by ops; same-key concurrent creation conflicts
roots.note: Two replicas that each assign `d.list = []` hold two distinct lists: one wins by op id, the other's items are hidden (reachable through `getConflicts`). The docs say to sync the initial change first or hard-code its bytes.

values.text: str, int, uint, f64, bool, null, `Date`, `Uint8Array`, `Counter`, `ImmutableString`
values.note: `bigint` is accepted (uint above i64 max) and reads back as a number when safe, as `bigint` from 2^53; NaN and Infinity round-trip as f64; `undefined`, functions, symbols and `Map` throw `RangeError`; class instances are stored as plain maps (all probed).
values.detail: A plain JS string becomes a collaborative text object (proxies.ts:201-202). Int/Uint/Float64 wrappers force a numeric type inside change(); inside from() they were stored as maps {value: n} (probed).

nestedPlain.text: becomes a nested map: its keys merge one by one; reassigning replaces it
nestedPlain.note: Assigning a whole new object creates a new map; a concurrent edit inside the old one is lost (probed: `o = {a: 9}` beat a concurrent `o.b = 3`).

kindClash.text: one wins by op id; the loser stays, readable through `getConflicts`
kindClash.note: The next write to the key resolves the conflict.
kindClash.detail: Probe: map {inner:1} at k (actor aaaa03) vs text at k (bbbb03) → text shown; getConflicts(m,'k') returned both, the map with its contents.

schema.text: none; `load<T>` trusts `T`, migrations are the app's job
schema.note: The docs name Cambria as research that is not implemented.

replicaId.text: actor ID: bytes (hex in JS), 16 random by default, app may set it
replicaId.note: One actor's changes must be sequential. 3.5.0 adds an optional `author` (hex) mapped to one or more actors.

idReuse.text: detected at merge: `duplicate seq N found for actor` error; no recovery
idReuse.note: Probe: two clones given one actor each made a change; `merge`, `applyChanges` and sync all threw `RangeError`. Nothing regenerates the id, and the two histories cannot be merged.

author.note: Stored in an actor's first change and kept through merge and save; changing the author mints a fresh actor.

opId.detail: A change is (actor, seq) and is addressed by the SHA-256 hash of its bytes.

clock.text: Lamport op counters (max seen + 1); causality via the change-hash DAG
clock.note: Reading at a version uses a per-actor vector of max op counters.

wallTime.text: per-change `time` (seconds), on by default; advisory, not in merge order

versionRepr.text: heads: an array of SHA-256 change hashes as hex strings
versionRepr.note: JSON-able as is; automerge-repo also encodes heads for URLs (`UrlHeads`).

versionCmp.text: `hasHeads(doc, heads)` tests inclusion; no ahead/behind/concurrent compare

map.text: JS object proxy: `d.k = v`, `delete d.k`; Rust `put`, `get`, `get_all`

lww.text: greater op id wins (counter, then actor); not wall-clock
lww.detail: Probe: a replica with one more prior op (higher counter) won with the lower actor id.

conflicts.text: `getConflicts(obj, key)` returns every concurrent value; Rust `get_all`
conflicts.note: Patches carry `conflict: true`; the next write to the key clears it.

deleteKey.text: `delete d.k`; a concurrent set beats the delete

clear.text: no clear op; delete keys one by one or reassign the parent
clear.note: Reassigning creates a new object, so concurrent writes into the old one are dropped.

keyOrder.text: sorted by key in the core; a live JS doc appends newly added keys
keyOrder.note: Probe: after a change `Object.keys` read `z, a, m`; after `load` it read `a, m, z`. Integer-like keys follow JS object rules.
keyOrder.detail: getBackend(doc).keys('_root') returned ['a','m','z']; uppercase sorted before lowercase (byte order). The read.rs doc comment does not state the order; the claim rests on the probe.

counterNum.text: 64-bit integer; decrement allowed; fractional deltas truncated
counterNum.note: `increment(1.7)` adds 1 and `new Counter(1.5)` stores 1 (probed). The sum is a plain i64 `+` with no overflow check.

counterReset.text: an overwrite or delete wins; concurrent increments are dropped
counterReset.note: An increment counts only while the counter's put has no other successor (probed: reset to 0 ‖ +3 → 0; delete ‖ +3 → key gone).

set.text: no set type; the docs give no set recipe
set.detail: Searched the docs clone for a set/map-keys recipe; none found.

listAlgo.text: RGA, as the docs name it; no paper cited

interleave.text: forward runs stay whole; runs typed backwards interleave element by element
interleave.note: Probe: per-keystroke appends `abc` ‖ `xyz` → `xyzabc`; per-keystroke prepends → `xaybzc` (lists too). The docs admit reverse insertion is not preserved.

listSet.text: `d.l[i] = v` writes in place; concurrent assigns conflict, op id wins
listSet.note: `getConflicts(list, i)` shows both; an assign concurrent with a delete revives the element (probed).

listMove.text: no move op; assigning an existing object elsewhere throws

listNested.text: lists hold maps, lists and texts at any depth

rle.text: columnar RLE/delta op columns, kept compressed in memory since 3.0

text.text: a JS `string` field is collaborative text; edit with `splice`, `updateText`

textAlgo.text: the same RGA as lists; marks follow Peritext

textUnits.text: UTF-16 code units in JS; Rust also offers code points, UTF-8, graphemes
textUnits.note: The WASM build hard-codes UTF-16; JS has no switch.

surrogates.text: an index inside a pair rounds to the whole character; never splits it
surrogates.note: Probe on `a😀b`: insert at 2 lands after 😀, `splice(1, 1)` removes 😀 whole; a lone surrogate inserted becomes U+FFFD.

splice.text: `splice(doc, path, index | cursor, del, text)`; negative `del` deletes backwards

updateText.text: `updateText(doc, path, s)`: Myers diff over grapheme clusters
updateText.note: Marked beta; the docs warn it merges poorly when called rarely. `updateSpans` diffs block structure but not marks.

delta.text: no Quill deltas; `spans()`/`updateSpans()` and patches instead

embeds.text: block markers (inline maps); `isEmbed: true` schema convention for images
embeds.detail: Probe: A.splice(d, ['t'], 1, 0, {x:1}) inserted nothing and did not throw; embeds go through splitBlock.

longText.text: every keystroke kept; a 260k-edit trace saves to 129 KB, loads in 0.13 s
longText.note: Our run, npm 3.5.0 under Node, on `rust/edit-trace/edits.json` in one change (5.6 s to apply). The 3.0 blog: pasting Moby Dick took 700 MB in 2.x and 1.3 MB in 3.0.
longText.detail: 259,778 edits → 104,852 chars; save() 129,100 bytes; load 132 ms; process RSS 312 MB at the end; stats numOps 182,316. benchmark-battery carries moby-dick.automerge and egwalker-paper traces.

marks.note: Mark values are scalars only (an object value throws).

markOverlap.text: one value per name per character; overlaps split, the greater op wins
markOverlap.note: Probe: `comment=c1` on 0–5 and `comment=c2` on 3–8 read back as c1 0–3 and c2 3–8; overlapping comments need distinct mark names.

unmark.text: `unmark(doc, path, range, name)`; against a concurrent mark, op id decides
unmark.note: An unmark is a null-valued mark, so per character the greater op id wins (probed: the concurrent unmark won on its range).

markWinner.text: per character, the greater op id (counter, then actor) wins
markWinner.detail: Probe: red on 0–6 (actor aa) ‖ blue on 3–11 (bb) → red 0–3, blue 3–11.

blocks.note: A published rich-text schema (`type`, `parents`, `attrs`, `isEmbed`) models nesting.

xml.text: no element tree type; block markers with `parents` paths instead

editors.note: Both are named by the docs and blog but are not in the clones; no Tiptap, Quill, Monaco, Lexical or Slate binding is named.

cursor.note: In JS cursors work on text only; the Rust core also takes lists.

cursorSide.text: anchored to the character at the index; `move` only sets the deletion fallback
cursorSide.note: Inserting at the cursor's index pushes it right (probed). `'start'`/`'end'` cursors stay pinned to the ends.

cursorDeleted.text: resolves to the next (`after`, default) or previous visible element
cursorDeleted.detail: Probe: cursor on 'w' of 'hello world' after deleting 'wor…': after → 7, before → 6.

txn.text: `change(doc, fn)` is one change: one hash, one callback; a throw rolls back
txn.note: Rust also offers an explicit `Transaction` with commit and rollback.

autoCommit.text: JS commits when the `change` callback returns; Rust `AutoCommit` before reads and saves
autoCommit.note: No timer; a callback with no ops makes no change.

commitMeta.note: Change metadata exposes `extraBytes` read-only; an author is stored in its actor's first change.

origin.text: the patch callback's `source` names the API call; no app-defined tag
origin.note: Sources include `change`, `merge`, `applyChanges`, `receiveSyncMessage`; the change `message` is replicated, not local.

multiDoc.text: no; a change belongs to one document

preCommit.text: no hook; a throw inside the `change` callback rolls it back

veto.text: `initSyncState({ readOnly: true })` ignores all of one peer's changes
veto.note: No per-change rule. On main only (unreleased), `maskAuthor(doc, author, heads)` hides an author's later changes in this replica's view.

events.text: `patchCallback` per call or per doc; automerge-repo `DocHandle` `change` events
events.note: No per-container observers in the core; automerge-repo `sub()` handles get scoped events.

eventBody.note: No raw bytes in the event; `getLastLocalChange()` returns them.

patches.text: `Patch[]` with paths, from callbacks and from `diff()`

applyPatches.text: `applyPatches(target, patches)`: to a plain object, or as ops inside `change`
applyPatches.note: A map-key `del` patch throws ('index is not a number for patch'), so round-trips that delete keys fail (probed).

pathSub.text: automerge-repo `handle.sub(...path)`: scoped handle with re-rooted patches (experimental)
pathSub.note: None in the core. The docs' Refs page (`handle.ref()`, `findRef`) describes an API the repo source at 3ab7c33 no longer has.

eventTiming.text: synchronously, after the commit, before the call returns
eventTiming.detail: Probed order: callback body, patchCallback, return.

historyKept.text: every change is kept; there is no history GC

historyList.note: `getHistory` and `topoHistoryTraversal` are `@hidden`; automerge-repo `handle.history()` lists heads in topological order.

timeTravel.text: `view(doc, heads)`: a cheap read-only doc at a version; Rust `*_at(heads)`

timeTravelNeeds.text: nothing: history is always whole; reads filter ops by a clock, no replay
timeTravelNeeds.note: `view` throws if a head is unknown.

versionDiff.text: `diff(doc, before, after)` → `Patch[]` between any two versions

revert.text: no revert API; `applyPatches(diff(now, past))` inside `change` is manual
revert.note: That recipe threw on a map-key deletion in our probe.

tags.text: no named versions; the app keeps heads itself

blame.text: no blame API; per-change `actor`/`author` metadata and `diff` per change
blame.note: 3.5.0 maps authors to actors (`getAuthors`, `getActorsForAuthor`); op ids name each value's actor (`getConflicts` keys).

trim.text: no shallow snapshot or history GC; compression keeps size down
trim.detail: Grepped rust/automerge/src for gc/shallow/truncate/compact: only save-format and patch-log uses.

purge.text: no; deleted content stays in the history on every replica
purge.note: `anonymize()` makes a scrubbed copy for sharing, not an in-place purge.

fork.text: `clone(doc)` copies with a new random actor; Rust `fork()`

detached.text: `view` is read-only; `changeAt(doc, heads, fn)` adds a change concurrent with later history

suggestions.text: `maskAuthor`/`revealAuthor` hide an author's changes in one view
suggestions.note: On main at 5bae775 only: not in the npm 3.5.0 build.

undo.text: no undo manager in the core or automerge-repo

format.text: binary columnar chunks: document, change, DEFLATE-compressed change, bundle
format.note: Each chunk: magic `85 6f 4a 83`, 4-byte checksum, type, length. Sync messages are v1 (`0x42`) or v2 (`0x43`); v2 may carry a whole document.

spec.text: published binary format spec on automerge.org (not in the clones)

snapshot.text: `save(doc)`: compressed doc with full history; no history-less save

mergeUpdates.text: saved chunks concatenate: `load(concat(a, b))` works; no compaction without loading
mergeUpdates.note: automerge-cli `merge` loads several files and writes one compacted document.

jsonExport.text: `decodeChange`/`encodeChange` (`@hidden`) map a change to and from JSON ops
jsonExport.note: automerge-cli `examine` prints changes as JSON; `export`/`import` move state, not changes.

fastLoad.text: columnar doc chunk; 3.0 keeps it compressed in memory; no change replay
fastLoad.note: Load verifies heads by default (hidden `unchecked` skips it). The 3.0 blog cites a 17-hour load cut to 9 s.

compat.text: 3.0 kept the 2.x file format; sync v2 still talks to v1 peers
compat.note: No written policy beyond 'we try and respect semver'; 0.11 began rejecting documents with misordered marks (`rescue` recovers their value).

syncProto.note: Based on arXiv:2012.00472; it assumes a reliable in-order stream.

reconnect.text: heads + a Bloom filter of changes since the shared heads + needs
reconnect.note: A persisted `SyncState` (`encodeSyncState`) keeps the shared heads across sessions; when over a third of the doc is due, v2 sends the whole compressed doc.

outOfOrder.text: queued until dependencies arrive; `getMissingDeps` lists them

duplicate.text: idempotent: deduplicated by hash, no patches emitted
duplicate.detail: Probed: applying the same change twice gave patches only the first time.

transport.text: bytes over any reliable channel; automerge-repo WebSocket, MessageChannel, BroadcastChannel
transport.note: No official WebRTC adapter in the clones.

server.text: `automerge-repo-sync-server` (reference, outside the clones): a plain `Repo`, validates nothing
server.note: The public `wss://sync.automerge.org` is not meant for production; Keyhive (alpha) adds an access policy for Subduction servers.

storage.text: automerge-repo IndexedDB and Node FS adapters over a key-range `StorageAdapter`
storage.note: Safe for concurrent writers: chunks are keyed by heads or hash, and compaction deletes only what it loaded.

awareness.note: `Presence` (heartbeats, per-peer state) ships in the 2.6 alphas.

hashes.text: SHA-256 change hashes; deps link them; heads checked on load

signatures.text: no signatures on changes in the core
signatures.note: Keyhive (alpha) signs sync traffic and contact cards, not individual changes; `emptyChange` is suggested for signing merged heads yourself.

checksums.text: each chunk carries a 4-byte SHA-256-prefix checksum, checked on load
checksums.detail: Probed: a flipped byte near the end of save() → RangeError 'bad checksum'.

malformed.text: undecodable bytes throw, nothing applied; nonsense ops panic and broke the doc
malformed.note: Probe: a change with an op on an unknown object (built with `encodeChange`) threw `PanicError` from Rust, via `applyChanges` and via a sync message; the same doc then panicked on its next `change`.
malformed.detail: Bad magic → RangeError 'Invalid magic bytes'; truncated change → 'unable to parse change'; a batch with one bad change applied nothing. After the panic: toJS still worked, A.change threw PanicError 'index out of bounds'.

bounds.text: 1 GB cap per decoded item, leb128 overflow checks; no queue or size caps
bounds.note: A libFuzzer target and crash fixtures (`too_many_ops`, `overflow_in_length`…) cover loading.

remoteValidation.text: none in the core; Keyhive's server policy (alpha) checks edit access only

e2ee.note: The docs say Keyhive is still in development and details will change.

fuzz.text: proptests, random fork/merge batch tests, a 3-repo fuzz, libFuzzer on `load`
fuzz.note: `write_frontier_parity` drives two peers and checks patches against hydrate and reload; the batch tests apply random edits from forks; the repo fuzz (3 repos, 100k changes) is a script, not CI.

proofs.text: no proofs or model checker; the sync code cites one paper
proofs.note: `sync.rs` names arXiv:2012.00472 as the protocol's basis; nothing about the CRDT is verified in the repo.
proofs.detail: Grepped the clones and docs for Isabelle/TLA+/proof/formal: none. Did not check the cited paper's content (offline).

errors.text: JS throws `RangeError` with messages; Rust has a typed `AutomergeError` enum
errors.note: Rust panics surface in JS as `PanicError`.

anonymize.text: `anonymize(doc)` replaces keys, values, actors and metadata, keeps history shape
anonymize.note: Best-effort, not cryptographic: the change graph, types, sizes and string lengths remain.

frameworks.text: react hooks, Svelte store, Solid primitives (automerge-repo packages); no Vue
frameworks.note: `@automerge/react` bundles the hooks with the repo and common adapters.

docs.text: automerge.org: tutorial, data model, merge rules, internals, cookbook, typedoc API
docs.note: The README calls the Rust API low level and not well documented; the binary format has its own spec page.

tests.text: Rust ~730 tests + proptests, JS 351, WASM 160, automerge-repo 711; GitHub CI
tests.note: CI builds and tests on Linux, macOS and Windows, runs the WASM and JS suites and a Node 18 packaging test; the C API has cmocka tests.
tests.detail: Counts by grep: 729 #[test] attributes in rust/automerge/src+tests; 351 it()/test() in javascript/test/*.ts (21 files); 160 it() in automerge-wasm/test/*.mts; 711 it()/test() across 37 *.test.ts files in automerge-repo/packages.

version.detail: Clone is main at 75e4bf2 (2026-10-23). The Rust crates `loro`/`loro-internal` are 1.17.1 too. npm `latest` = 1.17.1 per the brief (not checkable offline). The installed bench copy is 1.16.4; claims run against it are flagged in their cells.

status.detail: The CHANGELOG goes back to 0.6.0; the open-source announcement is dated 2023/11/13 and the v1.0.0 release 2024/10/21.

license.note: The licenses of `loro-prosemirror`, `loro-codemirror` and `loro-mirror` are not in the clones and were not checked.
license.detail: loro.js (pure TS port) is MIT too (loro/loro-js/package.json). The Loro Protocol repo (loro-websocket, loro-adaptors, Rust client/server) is MIT per its announcement post.

maintainer.text: Loro team (Zixuan Chen, Liang Zhao), GitHub org `loro-dev`
maintainer.detail: LICENSE: 'Copyright (c) 2023 Loro'. Funded through GitHub Sponsors of loro-dev (sponsorkit). npm package.json has an empty author.

impl.text: Rust core compiled to WASM with wasm-bindgen
impl.note: The same repo ships `loro.js`, an experimental pure-TypeScript port (0.4.0) that targets wire and API compatibility without WebAssembly.

deps.detail: package.json has only devDependencies (line 87 on). loro.js has none either.

wasm.text: required; entries load it sync (Node, browser), async (`web`) or inline (`base64`)
wasm.note: The default browser entry fetches the .wasm with a synchronous XMLHttpRequest. With the `bundler` entry, Vite needs `vite-plugin-wasm` and `vite-plugin-top-level-await`, and plain esbuild/Rollup must use `loro-crdt/base64` or copy the asset. The repo says nothing about CSP.
wasm.detail: Five builds: bundler, browser, nodejs, web, base64. The Node patch polyfills globalThis.crypto for getrandom (scripts/nodejs_patch.js). Bundle size in the benchmark table (1.0.0-beta.2): 2,919,363 bytes, 894,460 gzipped. A Rust panic or OOM traps the instance; the message lands in globalThis.__LORO_WASM_LAST_PANIC__ (src/lib.rs:94-140).

bindings.text: Rust `loro`, Swift `loro-swift`, Python `loro-py`; C# and Go by the community
bindings.note: Other bindings are built from `loro-ffi`, which is not in the clones. The repo also holds a MoonBit codec for the binary format (codec only) and the pure-TS `loro.js`.

runtimes.text: Node, browsers, Deno, Bun (all run in CI); no `engines` field
runtimes.note: The repo does not mention React Native / Hermes. The sync browser entry needs `XMLHttpRequest`; elsewhere use the `nodejs`, `web`, `base64` or `bundler` entry.
runtimes.detail: CI: Node 22.x, Deno v2, Bun 1.3.0, and Chromium runs of bundler smoke tests (Vite, Webpack, esbuild, Rollup, rsbuild, Next/Turbopack).

types.text: shipped .d.ts: wasm-bindgen output plus hand-written generics (`LoroDoc<T>`, `LoroMap<T>`)
types.detail: A `typescript_custom_section` in lib.rs carries the typed shape: `LoroDoc<T extends Record<string, Container>>`, `LoroMap<T>`, `LoroList<T>`, `LoroMovableList<T>`, `LoroTree<T>`; declarations of all five entries are checked with strict tsc (crates/loro-wasm/AGENTS.md).

apiStyle.text: mutable container handles; synchronous calls that throw on error
apiStyle.detail: `doc.getMap('m')` returns a handle (a new JS object each call). Containers can be built detached (`new LoroMap()`) and attached by `setContainer`/`insertContainer`. Nothing returns a promise (except loading the `web` entry).

unit.text: a `LoroDoc`: its op log (history) plus the state of named root containers
unit.detail: Each replica holds the whole document: OpLog (changes DAG) and DocState (current values).

manyDocs.text: one `LoroDoc` per document; no registry or subdocuments
manyDocs.note: The Loro Protocol multiplexes many documents (rooms) over one WebSocket, but the app still names and keeps them. A blog post says the team's directory CRDT (Flock) will be open-sourced later; it is not in the repo.

kinds.text: Map, List, MovableList, Text (rich text), Tree, Counter
kinds.detail: An `Unknown(u8)` kind keeps containers created by a newer version. Counter sits behind the `counter` cargo feature, which the WASM build enables.

nesting.text: Map, List and MovableList hold any container; each tree node holds a map
nesting.note: A child container gets a new id from the op that inserts it. Inserting an already-attached container copies it under a new id; no container moves between parents (tree nodes excepted).
nesting.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: list → list → map → text/tree → node map → counter works; `setContainer('b', attachedText)` produced a copy with a new cid.

roots.text: roots by name and type (`getMap("x")`) merge across replicas; children are minted by ops
roots.note: Root ids are `cid:root-<name>:<Type>`, so two replicas get the same root and a map named x never clashes with a text named x. A child from `setContainer` gets an op-based id; `ensureMergeable*(key)` gives a deterministic id so lazy concurrent creation merges.

values.note: A `Date` is stored as `{}`, bigint, functions and symbols throw, a JS `Map` becomes a map. Integers within ±2^53 are stored as i64, other numbers as f64.
values.detail: Checked with installed 1.16.4 (convert.rs not changed in the 1.17 CHANGELOG): undefined→null, Date→{}, 10n throws 'Unsupported value type', NaN/Infinity kept in memory, -0→0, Uint8Array round-trips.

nestedPlain.text: one atomic value, replaced whole by the map's LWW
nestedPlain.detail: A plain object becomes `LoroValue::Map`, stored as the key's value; setting an equal value is a no-op (lib.rs:7863-7864).

kindClash.text: Map LWW shows one; the loser stays readable by its container id
kindClash.note: The losing container is hidden (`isDeleted()` is true) but `getContainerById` still reads it. With `ensureMergeable*`, the losing kind's state resurfaces if that kind is ensured again.
kindClash.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: A setContainer(k, Map), B setContainer(k, Text), equal Lamport → both show the text (peer 2); getContainerById(cid:0@1:Map) returns the map {x:1} with isDeleted() true.

schema.text: none in core; `loro-mirror` declares a schema for its state view
schema.note: loro-mirror (official, not in the clones) maps a declared schema onto containers; the docs do not describe it rejecting remote data.

replicaId.detail: Exposed in JS as a decimal string (`${number}`). Every new LoroDoc gets a fresh id, even when loading the same document. `PeerID::MAX` is reserved.

idReuse.text: importing a clashing op id throws `UsedOpID`; nothing regenerates the id
idReuse.note: Detection happens only where the two histories overlap, at import; the import is refused and the document left unchanged. The docs make avoiding reuse the app's job.
idReuse.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: two docs with peer 7 inserting different text → import throws 'ID 0@7 has been used', state unchanged. Before 1.16.4 this trapped or scrambled text.

author.text: no: map peer ids to users, e.g. in `subscribeFirstCommitFromPeer`

opId.text: `{ peer, counter }` per op; each change also carries a Lamport
opId.detail: String form `counter@peer`; container ids (`cid:counter@peer:Type`) and tree node ids (`TreeID`) are op ids.

clock.text: Lamport; ties broken by larger peer id
clock.detail: `IdLp { lamport, peer }` derives Ord and 'is used to define the total order of Ops'. Version vectors/frontiers track causality.

wallTime.text: opt-in `setRecordTimestamp(true)`, in seconds; never used for merge order
wallTime.note: Off by default; a change then takes the largest timestamp seen. Timestamps are forced ascending and decide whether consecutive commits merge into one change.

lww.text: higher Lamport wins, then larger peer id; no wall clock
lww.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: concurrent set of k by peers 1 and 2 → peer 2's value.

conflicts.text: no; the losing values are reachable only through history
conflicts.detail: MapState holds one MapValue per key. Losers stay in the op log (checkout, exportJsonUpdates).

deleteKey.text: `map.delete(key)`; against a concurrent set, the same Lamport+peer LWW
deleteKey.detail: A delete is a MapSet with `value: None`, ordered like any other write.

clear.text: `map.clear()` writes one delete per present key
clear.note: Not a single reset op: keys a peer adds concurrently survive, and each deleted key races a concurrent set by LWW. `deleteRootContainer` empties and hides a root.

keyOrder.detail: Map state is a sorted SmallVec or BTreeMap; value snapshots use an FxHashMap. Checked on 1.16.4: keys() alphabetical, toJSON() hash order.

counterNum.text: f64 floats; decrement; no bounds or overflow checks

counterReset.text: no reset op; a concurrent increment lands in the deleted counter, hidden
counterReset.note: Rust `clear()` decrements by the observed value, so concurrent increments survive. Deleting the map key hides the counter; with `ensureMergeableCounter` re-ensuring resurfaces it with those increments.

set.text: no set type; map keys give LWW, not add-wins
set.detail: The docs do not prescribe a set model; a concurrent delete and re-add of a key resolve by Lamport+peer.

listAlgo.text: Fugue, merged by Eg-walker-style replay; MovableList moves per Kleppmann 2020
listAlgo.detail: Papers: Fugue arXiv 2305.00583; Eg-walker arXiv 2409.14252; 'Moving Elements in List CRDTs' (PaPoC 2020). The docs say Loro is 'not a strict implementation' of Eg-walker.

interleave.detail: Tests: forward (two peers typing), backward (typing at the start), mixed, and the Yjs anomaly case from the Fugue paper.

listRange.text: `delete(pos, len)` takes a range; `insert` takes one value per call
listRange.note: Many elements in one op only through `doc.applyDiff` with a list delta.

listSet.text: `LoroMovableList.set(i, v)`; concurrent sets keep one, by Lamport+peer

listMove.text: `LoroMovableList.move(from, to)`; the element stays once, last mover wins
listMove.detail: Checked on 1.16.4 too: concurrent moves of one element converge with it present once.

moveDelete.text: the move wins: the element comes back at its new place
moveDelete.note: A concurrent `set` and delete go the other way: the element stays deleted.
moveDelete.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: [x,y,z], A moves x to the end, B deletes x → both [y,z,x]; A sets x, B deletes x → [y].

rle.text: consecutive ops of one peer merge into runs and changes; columnar blocks
rle.detail: FugueSpan merges when peer, counter and lamport are contiguous; the `rle` crate drives op merging; history is stored as ~4 KB columnar ChangeBlocks.

textAlgo.text: same Fugue tracker as lists, Eg-walker-style replay; state in a B-tree rope
textAlgo.detail: ListDiffCalculator wraps the same RichtextTracker (FugueSpan rope) as RichtextDiffCalculator. Rich text styles follow Loro's Peritext-like design (blog/loro-richtext).

textUnits.text: UTF-16 by default; `insertUtf8`/`deleteUtf8` and `convertPos` for code points and UTF-8
textUnits.detail: TextPosType = 'unicode' | 'utf16' | 'utf8'. Cursor offsets are UTF-16 in JS. Storage is UTF-8.

surrogates.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: insert/delete at index 2 of 'a😀b' throws 'Cannot insert or delete utf-16 in the middle of the codepoint'.

updateText.note: Docs warn `update` can be slow past ~50,000 characters and point to `updateByLine`; a timeout throws.
updateText.detail: Diff in crates/loro-internal/src/diff/ (Apache-2.0 LICENSE there); `useRefinedDiff` option.

delta.detail: Quill-style insert/retain/delete with attributes; applyDelta pads with newlines when formatting past the end.

embeds.text: strings only; a delta insert must be text

longText.text: B-tree text, O(log n) edits; 260k-op trace: 231 KB, 6 ms parse
longText.note: The benchmark ran on 1.0.0-beta.2; 100× the trace (10.5M chars) gave 21 MB and 66 ms parse. Sequences are capped at about 1.07e9 items.
