longText.detail: B4 = automerge-perf trace (182k inserts, 77k deletes, 104,852 final chars). docSize 230,556 bytes, parseTime 6 ms, B4x100 docSize 21,016,454, parseTime 66 ms. Shallow snapshot of the same: 63 KB (docsize.md).

marks.note: A key needs a style config; unknown keys throw unless `configDefaultTextStyle` is set (bold, italic, underline, link, highlight, comment, code are preset).

markExpand.text: per key via `configTextStyle`: before, after, both or none
markExpand.detail: Not per mark call. Keys of the form `name:suffix` share the config of `name` (config.rs:40-50).

markOverlap.text: one value per key per character; `comment:<id>` keys overlap
markOverlap.note: Two `comment` marks over overlapping ranges leave the overlap with one value; distinct keys like `comment:1` and `comment:2` (sharing `comment`'s expand rule) both survive.
markOverlap.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: comment A on [0,7) and comment B on [4,11) concurrently → 'Hell' A, 'o World' B; with comment:1/comment:2 the overlap carries both. `configTextStyle` with a ':' in a key panics (traps the WASM).

unmark.text: `unmark(range, key)`; against a concurrent mark, Lamport+peer LWW
unmark.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: unmark by the larger peer erased a concurrent mark; by the smaller peer the mark survived.

markWinner.text: per character, higher Lamport then larger peer wins
markWinner.detail: StyleValue keeps a BTreeSet of StyleOps ordered by (lamport, peer) and reads `last()`. Checked on 1.16.4 in both peer orders.

blocks.text: no block markers; model blocks as containers
blocks.detail: loro-prosemirror maps ProseMirror's node tree onto Loro containers (not in the clones).

xml.text: no XML type; use Map, List or Tree

editors.note: Both are official loro-dev packages outside the clones. A Quill example lives in the repo (`examples/loro-quill`).

cursorDeleted.text: resolves to where it was, plus an `update` cursor on live content
cursorDeleted.note: Resolving a deleted anchor replays history, so storing the `update` cursor keeps later lookups fast.

fractional.note: A separate package in the same repo, not exported by `loro-crdt`.

treeCycle.text: Kleppmann 2021: moves applied in Lamport order, a cycle-making move is ignored
treeCycle.note: The loser's node stays where the other move put it; no event reports the dropped move.
treeCycle.detail: Retreat/replay window from the smallest differing lamport; `effected = false` when the target is an ancestor of the new parent. Checked on 1.16.4: A→B vs B→A converge with A under B.

treeOrder.text: ordered siblings by fractional index, on by default; `index()`
treeOrder.note: The tutorial says to call `enableFractionalIndex`, but the code and 1.16.4 have it on by default (jitter 0). Concurrent inserts at one spot can interleave, which the docs accept for trees.

treeDelete.text: `delete(id)` hides the subtree; a node moved into it is hidden too
treeDelete.note: A child moved out of a deleted subtree comes back. The deleted node itself cannot be moved; `revertTo` and undo re-create it with new ids.
treeDelete.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: concurrent delete(P) + move(X under P) → X deleted; local move of a child of a deleted node revived it; move(P) threw 'is deleted or does not exist'; revertTo and UndoManager.undo produced new TreeIDs.

txn.text: an implicit transaction closed by `commit()`: one event batch, one change
txn.note: Not ACID: there is no rollback, and an op that throws leaves earlier ops in place. Consecutive local commits can merge into one change (`setChangeMergeInterval`, default 1000 s).

autoCommit.text: on `commit()`, and implicitly before `import`, `export` and `checkout`; no timer
autoCommit.detail: Pending ops already update the local version; `getPendingTxnLength()` reports them.

commitMeta.text: `commit({ message, timestamp })`; the author is the peer id
commitMeta.note: No custom fields beyond the message string. `subscribePreCommit` can rewrite the message and timestamp.

origin.text: `commit({ origin })`: local only, in events and undo filters
origin.note: In JS `import()` takes no origin (Rust has `import_with`).

preCommit.text: `subscribePreCommit` edits message and timestamp; no veto
preCommit.detail: Ops made in `subscribeFirstCommitFromPeer` callbacks join the commit (lib.rs:6568-6597).

veto.text: no; imports get structural checks only

events.detail: A container subscriber also gets its descendants' events (dispatch walks ancestors, subscription.rs:101).

eventBody.text: per container: target, path, delta/map/tree/counter diff; from/to frontiers
eventBody.note: No old values, except a tree move's old parent and index. Update bytes come from `subscribeLocalUpdates`.

patches.text: events and `doc.diff()` give typed diffs with paths (not RFC 6902)
patches.detail: `diff(from, to, true)` returns JSON-safe diffs (`🦜:cid` strings for containers). loro-mirror turns them into immutable app state.

applyPatches.detail: `{ fullState: true }` aligns a `diff()` result with hidden mergeable children.

pathSub.detail: The callback gets no result; run `doc.JSONPath(path)` after it.

eventTiming.text: synchronously at the end of `commit`, `import` or `checkout` (since 1.8)
eventTiming.detail: Callbacks are queued and flushed by `callPendingEvents()` when the wrapped method returns; <=1.7 delivered on a microtask.

historyKept.text: every change kept; nothing is collected unless you export a shallow snapshot

timeTravelNeeds.text: history back to the target (not before a shallow root); replays only the ops between
timeTravelNeeds.detail: Checkout computes the diff from the current version to the target (retreat and forward), loading only the needed history blocks.

revert.text: `doc.revertTo(frontiers)` as new ops, all or nothing

blame.note: Attribution is by peer id; map peers to users yourself (e.g. with `subscribeFirstCommitFromPeer`).

trim.text: shallow snapshot drops history before chosen frontiers, like a Git shallow clone
trim.note: The trimmed doc cannot check out before its root, and rejects updates from peers whose edits are based on an older version.

purge.text: a shallow snapshot leaves deleted content out; other replicas keep theirs
purge.note: Only exported bytes are cleaned (reload from them), and deleted tree nodes' data stays because a later move can revive them. `redactJsonUpdates` blanks content in exported JSON updates.

fork.text: `doc.fork()` with a new random peer id

mergeBack.text: sync like any peer: `import(fork.export({ mode: "update", from }))`
mergeBack.detail: No dedicated merge call in JS; Rust tests use `LoroDoc::merge`.

detached.text: read-only unless `setDetachedEditing(true)`; edits then branch off
detached.note: Edits made while detached get a new peer id per checkout and form a concurrent branch; imports go to the log only until `attach()`.

suggestions.text: none; a fork merges back whole

undoLocal.text: tracks this doc's peer only; never undoes remote edits
undoLocal.note: Changing the peer id clears both stacks.

undoCursor.text: `onPush` returns cursors, `onPop` gets them back transformed

undoConflict.text: steps are transformed over remote edits (OT-style); remote inserts stay
undoConflict.detail: A step that became a no-op after remote edits is consumed and `undo()` returns false (CHANGELOG 1.17.0).

format.text: binary FastSnapshot and FastUpdates (modes 3, 4); JSON updates
format.detail: Modes 1–2 are pre-1.0 formats, still imported. Body: postcard + serde_columnar, LZ4-compressed SSTable blocks. JSON schema_version 1.

spec.text: `docs/encoding.md`, a normative spec, plus JSON, LZ4 and xxHash docs

snapshot.detail: Rust also has `StateOnly` and `SnapshotAt`. `LoroDoc.fromSnapshot(bytes)` loads one.

mergeUpdates.text: no; `importBatch` the blobs into a doc, then export
mergeUpdates.note: `decodeImportBlobMeta(bytes)` reads a blob's versions and mode without a doc.

jsonExport.detail: `exportJsonInIdSpan` exports one change deterministically (usable for hashing).

fastLoad.text: lazy ~4 KB compressed blocks, decoded on demand; columnar encoding
fastLoad.detail: The v1.0 post reports a 1.66M-op doc importing in 1.15 ms (vs 17.3 ms before), 375 µs as a shallow snapshot.

compat.text: stable since 1.0; older readers refuse newer encodings
compat.note: The decoder error says the format is backward compatible but not forward compatible; container kinds a reader does not know are kept as Unknown.

syncProto.text: none in core; the official Loro Protocol (`loro-websocket`, `loro-adaptors`)
syncProto.note: The protocol repo is not in the clones; this comes from its announcement post.

reconnect.text: version vectors; each side exports the ops past the other's vector

outOfOrder.text: held as pending until the deps arrive; `exportPendingUpdates()` saves them
outOfOrder.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: second update alone → pending {1: 5..6}; after the first arrives, 'hello!'.

duplicate.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: second import of the same bytes returned success Map(0) and fired no event.

transport.text: bytes over any transport; WebSocket client in `loro-websocket`

server.note: It validates only what its `authenticate` hook checks; persistence goes through `onLoadDocument`/`onSaveDocument`. Not in the clones.

storage.text: the app's job; docs give a snapshot plus updates recipe

awareness.detail: Default timeout 30 s; `subscribeLocalUpdates` for bytes; the older `Awareness` class is deprecated (index.ts:124-226).

partial.text: no; a peer receives the whole document
partial.detail: Exports select by version or op-id spans, never by container.

hashes.text: no; ops are named by peer and counter
hashes.note: The `subscribePreCommit` docs show building a Merkle DAG yourself by hashing `exportJsonInIdSpan` into the commit message.

checksums.text: xxHash32 over every blob, plus one per SSTable block
checksums.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: a flipped byte → 'Checksum mismatch. The data is corrupted.', doc unchanged.

malformed.text: throws; the import rolls back and the doc is unchanged
malformed.note: Many of these paths trapped the WASM instance until 1.16.4. A Rust panic still kills the instance (e.g. `configTextStyle` with ':' in a key).

bounds.text: decode caps (positions < 2^30, value depth 128); no size or pending caps
bounds.note: Nothing bounds the size of an update or the pending queue; a WASM out-of-memory traps the instance.
bounds.detail: Also MAX_COLLECTION_SIZE 2^28 for legacy decoding; iterative traversal for deep trees and values (CHANGELOG 1.17.0).

remoteValidation.text: no schema or rule checks; structural checks only

e2ee.text: experimental, in the Loro Protocol (`%ELO` rooms, `EloLoroAdaptor`)

fuzz.text: cargo-fuzz, 14 targets, 5 peers compared; loro.js-vs-Rust differential fuzz
fuzz.detail: Targets include tree, movable_list, mergeable, gc_fuzz, random_import, text-update, kv_store. Undo checks are in the fuzzer (undo.mdx:160-170).

proofs.text: none in the repo; docs cite the Fugue, Eg-walker and tree-move papers
proofs.note: The repo runs loom, a model checker for thread interleavings of the Rust doc, which tests thread safety rather than convergence.

errors.text: JS: thrown message strings, no class or code; Rust: typed `LoroError`
errors.note: In JS a `LoroError` becomes a plain string (no class or code); a few paths throw `Error`, and a Rust panic traps the instance.
errors.detail: Checked on 1.16.4: import of garbage and an out-of-bound insert throw `typeof 'string'`; cmpFrontiers on unknown frontiers throws an Error.

devtools.detail: Builds carry a DWARF-derived source map (README:104-110).

anonymize.text: `redactJsonUpdates` blanks content in JSON updates over a version range

frameworks.note: Official loro-dev packages outside the clones; no Vue, Svelte or Solid binding is named.

docs.text: loro.dev: tutorials, concepts, full JS API reference, benchmarks, blog
docs.detail: 17 tutorial, 15 concept, 7 advanced pages; js.mdx is ~6,600 lines; Rust docs on docs.rs; internals in repo docs/ and context/.

tests.text: ~2,000 Rust tests, 472 JS cases, 396 loro.js cases, fuzz, loom; CI
tests.source: loro/crates/loro-wasm/tests; loro/crates/loro/tests; loro/crates/loro-internal/tests; loro/loro-js/tests; loro/.github/workflows/rust.yml:13-68; loro/package.json:10-15
tests.detail: 1,994 #[test] across 269 Rust files; 53 vitest files in crates/loro-wasm/tests plus Deno and Bun suites; 41 loro.js test files. CI runs `deno task test-all` (nextest, WASM build+tests, loro.js, loom) on macOS.
